text: MSG-P7-009 is answered when a record carries a rule ID with no rule version or a decision code outside LOV-DECISION, with the field named in the problem detail; MSG-P7-012 is answered as a warning that names the chain_seq of an entry that does not verify; the rule-model refusal answers 422 with a problem whose messageId is left to the P7 message catalogue; the texts are filled in when the catalogue lands
why: The FSD names the two message IDs and the field they name but gives no text, and no source names the message of a refused rule-model read, so the story cannot write the wording or the status from the documents
read: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.3.1, A2.2.4.3 and A2.1.4.3; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 AC-EXC-P3-037-01; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 27
confirm: The solution architect and the P7 TechX squad publish the three texts and the refusal message ID in the P7 message catalogue before the SIT run
impact: No build blocker: the behaviour, the field name and the entry reference are fixed, the wording is a configuration change, and the tests assert the ID and the named field

text: The rule-model read is GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} and answers the compiled model of a version with packageCode, versionLabel, status, validFrom, checksum and model, only while the version is IN_FORCE and the stored SHA-256 matches; every other state and a checksum mismatch are refused rather than served
why: The architecture and the design give the owning services a model read on the hot path but the P7 API inventory holds no such operation and no source fixes the path parameters, the body or the refusal shape
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 27; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 and its notes; TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A.1; Template and Rules v1 DP-04 and DP-11
confirm: The solution architect confirms the published path, body and refusal in the rwb-decision OpenAPI document and the P7 appendix before the contract tests of wave 1
impact: The registry gate and the checksum check can be built and tested against the fixture now; a rename of the path or of a body field is a contract version change, not a redesign

text: The central entry holds the case reference as an opaque business key with no foreign key to rwb_case and no case attribute column, and the ALS business date is carried inside inputs_ref on the pattern of the FSD example inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a; the column change is agreed with the rwb_decision baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP
why: The TSD types the column as a uuid with a relationship to recovery_case and gives the row no business-date field, while the target forbids a cross-schema key and the legacy record must carry the ALS business date
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T3.3; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-008); legacy RWB-E1-018 flow step 11 and BR8; D-RCV-35 U4, ADR-010 and Template and Rules v1 DP-01
confirm: The solution architect and the P7 data owner confirm the column type and the business-date placement in the store story RWB-P7-E1008-APP before the wave-1 database build
impact: No build blocker: the index and the inputs reference work now; if the store story adds a business-date column, the tests read it there instead of inputs_ref and no scenario changes

text: The case-creation entry carries the rule ID that the published record carried for the ENTER row of package ENTRY, together with rule version ENTRY-2026.11; the story asserts its presence and its equality with the record and never a literal
why: The legacy story requires the ENTER rule ID on every case-creation record and the design says the rule ID is the fired row name, but no source lists an ENTRY row name, and inventing one would put a business value into the test data and the code
read: Legacy RWB-E1-018 flow step 7, BR8 and section 11; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16; legacy AC2 and AC6 for the EXCLUSION naming pattern
confirm: The center of excellence analyst publishes the ENTRY Rows tab with its rule IDs in RWB-P7-E1073-APP
impact: No build blocker: the mapping is a copy of the record field, and the literal lands in the registry and the fixture when the package is published
